## Appearance

Anne is a tall and slender girl with a milk-white skin, a slim throat, and a pointed, freckled face. She possesses solemn, luminous gray eyes, which are sometimes described as gray-green, set above a pointed chin and a nicely shaped, freckled nose. Her hair, which friends call auburn, is notably red and has been worn in long braids, shingled closely, and left unbraided in a torrent of brightness. She has an expressive face with delicate features, pale cheeks that faintly flush with pink, and an overall bright, animated appearance.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER V. Anne’s History P0](../source/v01-c05.md#nw-v01-c05-p0000), [v1 CHAPTER VII. Anne Says Her Prayers P12](../source/v01-c07.md#nw-v01-c07-p0012), [v1 CHAPTER VIII. ## Personality

Characterized by an intensely passionate nature, she holds tight to both her loves and her hatreds while possessing an unpraiseworthy tendency to harbor grudges. Though once notably talkative, stubborn, and prone to reckless impulsiveness, she gradually grew much quieter over time. She is remarkably smart, idealistic, and deeply imaginative, approaching life with an innate poetic optimism despite taking things quite seriously. Driven by a desire to bring beauty to the world and pursue higher education, she aims to serve as a supportive teacher who truly helps her pupils. Beyond her scholarly ambitions, she possesses a natural talent with children, a good singing voice, and practical knowledge like treating croup. However, she struggles with a fear of being alone and was once terrified of passing through the [Haunted Wood](../codex/places.md#haunted-wood) after dark.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P3](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P18](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0018), [v1 CHAPTER VI. ## History

Born in [Bolingbroke](../codex/places.md#bolingbroke), [Nova Scotia](../codex/places.md#nova-scotia), Anne Shirley was orphaned as an infant and raised by Mrs. [Thomas](../character/thomas-lynde.md), Mrs. [Hammond](../character/hammond.md), and an asylum before [Matthew Cuthbert](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) brought her to [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F9]. Upon her arrival, she broke into tears when [Marilla Cuthbert](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) expressed shock that she was not a boy, though [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) ultimately decided to raise her [S1, S3]. In [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea), Anne swore eternal friendship with [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md), a bond that survived a temporary ban after Anne accidentally served [Diana](../character/diana-barry.md) home-made currant wine [S9, S15, S17]. At school, she smashed her slate over [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) Blythe's head after he taunted her red hair, igniting a prolonged academic rivalry [S13, S40]. Following Matthew's sudden death, Anne gave up her college scholarship to stay home, care for Marilla's failing eyes, and teach locally, reconciling with [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) after he gave up the [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school for her [S42, S43]. While teaching, she helped found the Village [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers) and convinced [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) to take in the orphaned twins [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md) Keith [S45, S51]. Later, after earning her degree at [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college), she rejected a proposal from [Roy Gardner](../character/roy-gardner.md) before accepting Gilbert's proposal in Hester Gray's garden [S115, S117]. The couple married and moved to [Four Winds Harbor](../codex/places.md#four-winds-harbor), where Anne formed deep friendships with Captain Jim and their tragic neighbor [Leslie Moore](../character/leslie-moore.md) [S120, S121, S130]. After the heartbreaking loss of her first baby, Joyce, Anne gave birth to a healthy son, [James Matthew](../character/james-matthew.md) [S138, S140, S153]. Eventually, after Captain Jim's peaceful death, Anne and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) prepared to move to the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen), comforted that [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) and her new husband would purchase their beloved home [S158, S159].

## Quotes

> "Pretty well. I’m better at looking after children, though. I’ve had so much experience at that. It’s such a pity you haven’t any here for me to look after."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P24](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0024)

> “I think he’s lovely,” said Anne reproachfully. “He is so very sympathetic. He didn’t mind how much I talked—he seemed to like it. I felt that he was a kindred spirit as soon as ever I saw him.”
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P26](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0026)

> "Oh, I don’t mean that sort of a name. I mean just a name you gave it yourself. Didn’t you give it a name? May I give it one then? May I call it—let me see—Bonny would do—may I call it Bonny while I’m here? Oh, do let me!"
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER IV. Morning at Green Gables P33](../source/v01-c04.md#nw-v01-c04-p0033)

> "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P11](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0011)

> "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"
>
> — Anne Shirley — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P43](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0043)

## Relationships

### [Allan](../character/allan.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/allan--anne-shirley.md)

Mrs. Allan is the local minister's wife, a Sunday school teacher, and a valued friend who acts as an extra conscience for Anne. Their bond began during a memorable tea party where Anne accidentally flavored a cake with anodyne liniment instead of vanilla, but Mrs. Allan treated her with gentle kindness. Over the years, they have shared deep conversations on faith, sorrow, teaching ideals, and the value of friendship.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings P0](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0000), [v1 CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v1 CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings P6](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0006), +26 more_

### [Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--diana-barry.md)

[Diana Barry](../character/diana-barry.md) is Anne's closest childhood friend and schoolmate, with whom she swore eternal friendship shortly after moving to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea). Together, they have shared countless imaginative adventures, co-founded the local [Improvement Society](../codex/factions.md#improvers), and stood by each other through childhood mishaps and life milestones. Their bond is grounded in mutual devotion, surviving early social obstacles and family misunderstandings to remain steadfast as they grow into adulthood.
